problem: Teleoperation world models mix action-selection style, shared action-conditioned dynamics and camera/appearance changes; adapting an entangled predictor can corrupt dynamics rather than repair the relevant interface.
contribution: An explicit causal factorization and intervention protocol distinguish operator habit, physics and visual nuisance, accompanied by freeze-versus-finetune-versus-scratch adaptation tests and negative boundary cases.
algorithm: Factor actions as a=g(h,z,u), dynamics as z'=f(z,a), observations as o=r(z,c). Probe action substitutions at fixed state and appearance/viewpoint changes. Train joint-facing proprioceptive or pixel dynamics; freeze the shared readout while fitting a thin interface when exclusion assumptions hold. Combine physics likelihood and a habit prior to rank candidate past transitions.
observations: ManiSkill StackCube latent/state variables; DROID/RH20T joint/action transitions; DROID exterior RGB with one training view and a second-view evaluation. Pixel predictions are supervised by current/next joints rather than video realism alone.
actions: Recorded executed/commanded dataset actions under the paper's source conventions; controlled action shuffles, same-task user swaps, zero actions and deliberately scaled adaptation commands. Latent actions recovered from video are explicitly not equated with operator habit.
embodiment_and_data: Simulation Physical Kernel on StackCube, public DROID and multi-operator RH20T offline corpora. Closed-loop success evidence is simulated; the paper explicitly leaves robot hardware deployment open.
experiments: Interventions, low-shot adaptation, corrupted demos, multi-step prediction, cross-camera/appearance shifts, reverse ranking and a limited StackCube closed-loop check. Experiments also expose failed simulator-to-DROID frozen representations, coarse command interfaces, over-aggressive action hinges and weak cross-task style transfer.
baselines: Frozen dynamics plus small interface, joint finetuning, scratch learning, entangled next-image prediction, correct/wrong habit priors, and an external DreamZero-style model with base/LoRA/kernel-bridge probes. External action-model probes are boundary experiments rather than the proposed method.

quantitative_result.source: PDF page4 TableIV and page3 StackCube closed-loop text
quantitative_result.conditions: StackCube adaptation N=128, eight seeds, evaluation described as40episodes. DROID pixel quantities use seeds0,1,2. These diagnostics and simulation successes are not physical robot results.
quantitative_result.caveat: Page5 TableV is seed0; its N=32 freeze0.22 is not the three-seed0.194±0.018 mean reported elsewhere.

limitations: Causal exclusions depend on sufficiently informative state and on habit not directly changing physical parameters. Interventions are proxies; action sensitivity alone can be gamed by the training objective. Frozen simulator representations are weak on DROID, cross-camera change is harder than color jitter, cross-task habit results are inconclusive, and reverse scores are not reliable operator identification. No hardware validation is reported.
hardware_adaptation: ADAPT intervention-based diagnosis and frozen-interface ablations to logged SO-101 measurements first. ROSMASTER lacks measured arm readback, so a joint-facing target cannot be fabricated from its command estimate. Verify the actual downstream policy consumes the dynamics factor before attributing performance to it.
algorithm_detail: The pixel model uses j_hat=probe(Enc(o)) and next-joint residual delta(Enc(o),a), plus a wrong-action hinge and optional appearance consistency. Training only latent consistency can collapse to action-insensitivity. Moderate hinges preserve adaptation; maximizing intervention ratios alone can harm low-shot performance. Thin-interface reuse is justified by an evaluated SCM, not a universal frozen-physics premise.
integration_contract: Record actor/task identity separately from observed state, dispatched action and camera nuisance. Use session-disjoint splits; apply counterfactual action perturbations offline. Log intervention type and target metric. A new user/camera does not authorize changing physical calibration, and a failed interface does not imply the shared dynamics are wrong.
license_evidence: The primary six-page PDF was examined through its method, tables and limitations; no software-license grant or audited code repository is established by that text. Offline corpus licenses remain separate.
required_experiments: Action shuffle versus nuisance edits with true measured-state targets; freeze/finetune/scratch at equal shot budgets; evaluate both diagnostic ratio and actual adaptation error; test in-domain versus transplanted representations; include a downstream ablation that scrambles the supposedly used dynamics factor.
difference_from_explorer: This is close prior work for selective repair and habit/physics/nuisance attribution. Explorer cannot claim that factorization or freeze-and-adapt prescription as new; its contribution would need broader retained-skill/embodiment/handover evaluation and actual validated use of diagnostic outcomes.
